DILG Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 11 s. 2022 FEB 17 2022 Hon. TEOTIMO F. FAMPULME JR. Chairperson Committee on Rural and Urban Development Sangguniang Bayan of Gloria Batasang Pambayan Rizal Street, Maligaya, Gloria Oriental Mindoro sangguniangloria@gmail.com Dear Hon. Fampulme: This refers to your Indorsement letter dated 01 December 2021 with attached Committee Report No. 01 -2021 (Committee Report) requesting for the Department's legal opinion on the following issues concerning the Balete Core Housing Project (Housing Project) of Barangay Balete (Balete) located in Barangay Sta. Theresa (Sta. Theresa): I. Ang Barangay Balete ay bumili ng Iupa sa nasasakupan ng Barangay Sta. Theresa para sa kanilang "Pabahay Project para sa mga Mahihirap" na kanilang pinamamahalaan at pinupondohan mula taong 1995. Sino ngayon ang barangay na nakakasakop sa Balete Core Housing? Barangay Balete ba o Barangay Sta. Theresa? 2. Sinong Sangguniang Barangay ang dapat mamahala sa Balete Core Housing na matatagpuan sa Barangay Sta. Theresa? Barangay Balete ba o Barangay Sta. Theresa? 3. Dahil ang mga nakatira sa Balete Core Housing ay mula lahat sa Barangay Balete at iginigiit na sila ay taga-Barangay Batete, kanino sila kukuha ng Barangay/Business Clearance? Sa Barangay Balete ba o sa Barangay Sta. Theresa? 4. May karapatan ba ang Sanggunlang Barangay ng Balete na bumahagi sa local income ng Balete Core Housing kahit na ito ay matatagpuan sa Barangay Sta. Theresa? The same Committee Report was likewise endorsed on 03, 07, and IO December 2021 by Mr. Ricardo C. Santos, MLGOO of DILG Gloria; Dir. Maria Victoria J. Dei Rosario, Provincial Director of DILG Oriental Minodoro; and Dir. Wilhelm M. Suyko, Regional Director of DILG MIMAROPA Region. Per the attached Committee Report, both Balete and Sta. Teresita are barangays located within the Municipality of Gloria, Mindoro (Gloria). Sometime in 2015, Balete identified private parcels of land located in Sta. Theresa with the intention of establishing the Housing Project for Balete's less fortunate constituents. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

In 2016, Gloria's Municipal Appraisal Committee issued Resolution 2016-121 Authorizing the Sangguniang Barangay of Balete to negotiate and purchase the identified parcels of land located in Sta. Theresa. The Resolution stated that Sta. Theresa authorized Balete's purchase of the same. By 2021, Balete has duly purchased the identified parcels of land, and is processing the transfer of titles under its name. Sta. Theresa, however, issued Resolution No. 23, series of 2021 requesting from Gloria to take over the Housing Project, and to impart upon the residents of the Housing Project that they are under the jurisdiction of Sta. Theresa, not Balete. This Department respectfully submits that Sta. Theresa has the authority to exercise the powers and functions of a barangay within the Housing Project which includes the issuance of barangay certificates. Meanwhile, the residents of the Housing Project shall vote in the precinct where they are duly registered under the rules of COMELEC. We differentiate property ownership from territorial jurisdiction by a local government unit (LGU). Under Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code (LGC), an LGU is likewise a corporation which may, in its' private capacity, acquire and convey real or personal property. 1 It may therefore act akin to a private corporation, and purchase or sell real and personal property wherever the same be located. Meanwhile, territorial jurisdiction refers to the territorial boundaries as delineated by law, such as the LGU's charter.2 It is the area wherein an LGU has the obligations, responsibilities, and powers of government unit as stated under the LGC. In the case of Municipality of Isabel, Leyte vs. Municipality of Merida, Leyte3, the Supreme Court held as follows: "Precision in the delineation of local govemment unit boundaries is of immense importance because these boundaries determine the spatial extent of the powers of local government units. A local government unit can legitimately exercise governmental powers only within its territorial jurisdiction. Outside these geographical bounds, the acts of local government units are ultra vires. Likewise, it has been observed that: [t]he inhabitants residing within [the territorial] area [of a LGU] are invested with certain municipal liberties, rights and privileges. They are also impressed with certain duties and obligations. x x x It is thus obvious that every municipal corporation must have its boundaries fixed, definite and certain as to precise location, in order that they may be identified, and that all may know the exact scope or section of territory or geographical division embraced within the corporate limits, and over which the local corporation has jurisdiction. To aid the duly designated tribunals in the task of boundary dispute resolution, the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Local Government Code require the submission inter alia of the following: a duly authenticated copy of the law or statute creating the LGU or any other document 2 3 Section 22 (4), Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code. Republic of the Philippines vs. Provincial Government of Palawan, G.R. No. 170867 dated 04 December 2018, Municipality of Isabel, Leyte vs. Municipality of Merida, Leyte, G.R. No. 216092 dated 09 December 2020 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

showing proof of creation of the LGU; a provincial, city, municipal, or barangay map, as the case may be, duly certified by the Lands Management Bureau; technical description of the boundaries of the LGU is concerned; written certification of the provincial, city, or municipal assessor, as the case may be, as to territorial jurisdiction over the disputed area according to records in custody; and written declarations or sworn statements of the people residing in the disputed area." Based on the foregoing, an LGU, in its private capacity, may own parcels of land wherever the same is located. It may, however, only exercise governmental functions within the its territorial jurisdiction. For barangays, such territorial jurisdiction may be delineated pursuant to the charter of the barangay, a barangay map duly certified by the Land Management Bureau, among others. Presently, Balete, as corporation, may purchase the private property identified for its Housing Project. The titles, once issued, shall be under the name of Balete. The latter may then exercise the rights of an owner under the New Civil Code, including allowing their constituents to reside in the same, or eventually sell the properties under reasonable terms. The Housing Project, however, is physically located within the territorial jurisdiction of Sta. Theresa. Verily, it is Sta. Theresa which may exercise governmental functions related to the same, including the issuance of barangay certificates. We respectfully manifest that at present, our jurisprudence does not recognize the unilateral expansion of an LGU's territorial jurisdiction through the purchase of private land located in a different jurisdiction. Otherwise, affluent LGUs would simply purchase parcels of land of poorer LGUs in order to gain more political and territorial power, regardless of whether they can deliver basic services to their constituents in far flung areas. This Department, however, understands that Balete seeks to be more active in the service of persons in the Housing Project. Hence, it is strongly recommended that Balete and Sta. Theresa enter into a Memorandum of Agreement, and cooperate for the betterment of the residents of the Housing Project in accordance with the LGC, as follows: "Section 33. Cooperative Undertakings Among Local Government Units. - Local govemment units may, through appropriate ordinances, group themselves, consolidate, or coordinate their efforts, services, and resources for purposes commonly beneficial to them. In support of such undertakings, the local government units involved may, upon approval by the sanggunian concerned after a public hearing conducted for the purpose, contribute funds, real estate, equipment, and other kinds of property and appoint or assign personnel under such terms and conditions as may be agreed upon by the participating local units through Memoranda of Agreement." Lastly, we respectfully submit that a person's voter registration is not automatically transferred upon a person's relocation to different territorial jurisdiction. The residents of the Housing Project who came from Balete are therefore still registered voters of the said barangay, unless they transfer their registration in accordance with the rules of COMELEC. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to •ently addressed your concerns. Thank you.
